A1.situation: At the flower shop, you want some red flowers. What do you say?
Your uncle is at your door. It is cold outside. What do you say?
In a taxi, you want to go to the airport. What do you tell the driver?
Your teammate wants your phone number. What do you tell him?
You want to know the weather for tomorrow. What do you ask your dad?
It is your first English class. What do you say to the teacher?
Lily shows you a photo of her new puppy. What do you say?
At a kiosk, you want a bottle of cold water. What do you say?
Your bus is slow this morning. What do you tell your boss on the phone?
Ben wants to play tennis on Saturday. You are free. What do you tell him?
At the market, you want one kilo of tomatoes. What do you say?
On Monday, a colleague asks about your weekend. What do you tell her?
At a party, you want to dance with Mia. What do you ask her?
A nice song is on the radio. What do you ask your friend about it?
Your grandfather is tired. You want to help him. What do you say?
You see an old school friend in the street. What do you say to him?
Your dad asks what you would like for breakfast. What do you tell him?
Your colleague likes your new shirt. What do you say to him?
You want to watch TV, but your sister is reading. What do you ask her?
A new classmate asks what you like to do at weekends. What do you say?
At the sandwich bar, you want one with cheese and tomato. What do you say?
Your friend comes to your house. She is thirsty. What do you ask her?
You want to learn to swim. What do you ask at the pool?
Your class has a test tomorrow, and Sara is worried. What do you tell her?
Your neighbour is moving to another city. What do you say on her last day?
Your teacher asks why you are happy today. What do you say?
You want to know the bus number for the city centre. What do you ask?
Your grandad bakes you a cake. What do you tell him?
You want to open the window in the office. What do you ask your colleague?
It is late, but your cousin wants another film. What do you tell him?
You cannot find the exit in a big shop. What do you ask a shop assistant?
You want a hot chocolate with no sugar. What do you say to the waiter?
Your colleague goes on holiday tomorrow. What do you say to him?
A woman in the lift asks which floor you want. What do you say?
You want a boat for an hour on the lake. What do you ask?
Your son wins a prize at school. What do you say to him?
You do not know a word in your book. What do you ask your mum?
At the beach, you want to rent two chairs. What do you ask?
Your new phone is hard to use. What do you ask your brother?
Your niece is in a school play tonight. What do you say to her?
You want a smaller size of these jeans. What do you ask the assistant?

A2.situation: You want to book a hotel room for two nights next month. What do you say on the phone?
Your brother starts university next month and feels nervous. What do you say to him?
You bought a ticket for the wrong train. What do you say to the ticket inspector?
You want to join a dance class, but you don't know the times. What do you ask?
Your colleague brought cakes to work for her birthday. What do you say to her?
You arrived at the airport and your bag did not come. What do you say at the desk?
You want to borrow your friend's tent for a camping trip. What do you ask him?
You want a refund for a concert that was cancelled. What do you say on the phone?
Your sister asked you to help paint her room on Saturday. What do you say?
You want to change tomorrow's boat trip because of the weather. What do you ask the company?
Your teacher asked the class for ideas for a school trip. What do you suggest?
You want to send some money to your brother. What do you ask at the bank?
You met a woman last week, but you forgot her name. What do you say?
You need a new key for your flat. What do you ask your landlord?
A colleague invited you for lunch, but you already ate. What do you say?
You like some boots in the window and want to try them on. What do you ask?
You are going to visit a friend's city for the first time. What do you ask her?
Your friend asks about the film you saw last night. What do you tell him?
The coffee machine at work is broken again. What do you tell the office manager?
You want to sell your old bike. A neighbour asks about it. What do you say?
Your sister wants to go shopping on Saturday, but you will be working. What do you tell her?
In a big museum, you are looking for the gift shop. What do you ask a guard?
You want to know how much a weekly gym pass costs. What do you ask at reception?
Your host is cooking dinner and asks if you want to help. What do you say?
You arrived early for a meeting, and the room is empty. What do you ask the receptionist?
You cannot come to football practice tomorrow. What do you tell your coach?
A new colleague does not know where the meeting room is. What do you say to her?
You want to change your hotel room because it is too noisy. What do you say at reception?
Your washing machine is making a strange noise. What do you say when you call the repair service?
You want to know if the restaurant has vegetarian dishes. What do you ask when you call?
Your phone plan is too expensive. What do you ask the phone company?
You lost your library card last week. What do you say to the librarian?
Your cousin is nervous before his first driving lesson. What do you say to him?
You want to plant flowers in the garden of your building. What do you ask your neighbours?
You are meeting a friend at the station, but you can't find her. What do you say when you call?
You found a great new cafe yesterday. What do you tell your friend about it?
You need help to finish a report by Friday. What do you ask your colleague?
You want to take your dog on the train. What do you ask at the ticket office?
Your sports club is having a party. What do you say to invite a new member?
You are on a plane and want a blanket. What do you say to the flight attendant?
You want to know when the next ferry leaves. What do you ask at the port?

B1.situation: You are on a business trip and your hotel booking has disappeared from the system. What do you say to the receptionist?
Your cousin has asked you to be the photographer at her small wedding, but you aren't very experienced. What do you say?
Your colleague often leaves the kitchen at work untidy, and it's starting to annoy everyone. What do you say to him?
You've just moved in and want to get to know the family next door. What do you say when you knock?
Your evening course has moved to a time you can't make, and you'd like a solution. What do you tell the college?
A tourist asks you to recommend somewhere to spend a rainy afternoon in your city. What do you suggest?
You have been chosen to welcome visitors from a partner company at the airport. What do you say when you meet them?
Your housemate keeps eating your food without asking, and you've run out of milk again. What do you say to her?
You are buying a second-hand washing machine, and you want to check that it works properly. What do you ask the seller?
Your manager has asked for volunteers to organise the end-of-year party, and you'd like to help. What do you say?
At the concert entrance, the ticket on your phone won't load. What do you say to the staff?
You'd like a part-time job at your local bookshop. What do you say when you speak to the manager?
A friend wants to go on holiday with you, but she prefers beaches and you prefer mountains. What do you suggest?
You've been asked to explain a new recycling system to the people in your building. What do you say at the meeting?
Your car won't start this morning, and you need to get to an important meeting. What do you tell your manager?
You want to bring a friend to your gym, but you're not sure about the rules. What do you ask at reception?
Your teenage nephew wants advice about choosing subjects for next year. What do you say to him?
You gave your sister a cooking class as a gift, but she can't make the date. What do you tell the school?
You've been waiting for twenty minutes in a restaurant and nobody has taken your order. What do you say to the waiter?
A colleague from abroad is visiting your office and wants to try local food. What do you suggest?
You are moving house next week and need to stop your internet contract. What do you say when you call the provider?
Your neighbour has started a small online shop and asks you to share it with others. What do you say?
You've noticed that a new colleague eats lunch alone every day. What do you say to invite her to join you?
The neighbours above you often move furniture late at night. What do you say when you meet them on the stairs?
You are planning a surprise party for your colleague and need help from her husband. What do you say when you phone him?
You want to rent a car for a weekend trip, and you need a child seat. What do you ask at the counter?
Your study partner wants to stop meeting because she has found a part-time job. What do you say to her?
You are at a farmers' market and want to know how the cheese was made. What do you ask the seller?
Your team is planning a charity run, and you need to persuade colleagues to take part. What do you say at the meeting?
You've lost your hotel key card and you're locked out of your room late at night. What do you say at reception?
A friend asks whether she should buy a new laptop now or wait for the sales. What do you say?
You want to cancel your gym membership, but the staff keep offering you deals. What do you say?
Your aunt has arrived for a visit, but your flat isn't ready because you've been working late. What do you say to her?
The swimming pool you use has become very crowded in the evenings. What do you suggest to the manager?
A delivery driver phones because he can't find your house, which is hidden from the road. What do you say?
You are at a job fair and want to find out about training opportunities at one company. What do you ask the representative?
Your colleague's presentation went very well, but she seems unsure about it. What do you say to her?
You've been invited to speak at your old school about your job. What do you say at the start of your talk?
You've been asked to choose a restaurant for a team dinner, and people have different tastes. What do you suggest to the team?
A neighbour asks if you'd like to share a vegetable garden in the back yard. What do you say?
Your train is cancelled, and you want to suggest sharing a taxi with a stranger going the same way. What do you say to her?

B2.situation: Your manager wants you to train new staff, although it isn't part of your role. What do you say?
A client has asked you to lower your fee because her budget has been cut. What do you say?
You've been offered two jobs and must explain to one company why you're declining. What do you say?
A neighbour has complained that your children play too loudly in the garden. What do you say to him?
Residents are being consulted about building flats on a local field. What do you say at the meeting?
A colleague has asked you to cover for him while he leaves early every Friday. What do you say?
Your teenage son wants to take a gap year before university. What do you say to him?
A hotel guest is unhappy that the pool has been closed for maintenance. What do you say to her?
You were promised a refund within a week, but a month has passed. What do you say when you call?
A customer is asking for information you're not allowed to share. What do you say to him?
Your landlord wants to sell the flat and asks you to move out early. What do you say?
You need to persuade your team to try a new way of planning projects. What do you say?
A colleague asks whether you'd recommend her for a role in your department. You have doubts. What do you say?
Your boss suggests moving the conference online, which many attendees would find disappointing. What do you say?
A university student asks to interview you about how you built your career. What do you say?
You've been told that a project you worked hard on is being cancelled. What do you say to the director?
Your book group wants to read only bestsellers, and you'd like more variety. What do you say?
A courier left your parcel with a neighbour you've never met. What do you say when you knock?
Your company's new open-plan office makes it hard for you to concentrate. What do you suggest to HR?
A tour guide's schedule leaves no free time, and the group is getting tired. What do you say to her?
You're asked at an interview to describe a time when you made a mistake. What do you say?
A colleague has been asked to give a speech at short notice and is nervous. What do you say to her?
Your football team has lost five matches in a row, and morale is low. As captain, what do you say?
A supplier has quoted a price that is much higher than last year. What do you say to the account manager?
You realise you've double-booked a meeting with an important client. What do you say when you call her?
A close friend has been offered a job abroad but is afraid of leaving her family. What do you say to her?
You think the company website is confusing for customers. What do you say to the marketing team?
A hotel has given away the room you reserved and paid for. What do you say to the manager?
Marathon organisers have changed the route at the last minute. As a runner, what do you say to them?
A new employee asks how to make a good impression in her first month. What do you say?
You've been asked to explain why your team should get a new piece of equipment. What do you say?
A former colleague has invited you to join her start-up, but you're happy in your current job. What do you say?
A theatre has cancelled the show you had tickets for, offering only a voucher. What do you say?
Your partner's parents are visiting, and they'd like to stay longer than planned. What do you say?
A colleague is spreading a rumour about upcoming changes in the company. What do you say to him?
Your neighbour has parked across your driveway again. What do you say when you see him?
One learner in the evening course you teach constantly checks her phone during lessons. What do you say to her?
The insurance company has rejected your claim for a damaged suitcase. What do you say when you call?
Your company is considering cutting the training budget. What do you say to defend it?
You'd like to start an hour earlier and finish earlier each day. What do you say to your manager?
A cafe owner asks what you think of her new menu, which you find disappointing. What do you say?

C1.situation: A senior colleague has asked you to sign off on figures you haven't had time to verify. What do you say?
You've been asked to persuade a reluctant team to adopt a new performance review system. What do you say?
A long-term client has started bypassing you and contacting your junior staff directly. What do you say to her?
A friend has asked you to be a referee for a job you think she's unsuited to. What do you say?
You must explain to your team why a much-anticipated bonus scheme has been postponed. What do you say?
A visiting lecturer has run well over time, and the next speaker is waiting. As chair, what do you say?
An applicant you interviewed asks for detailed feedback on why she was unsuccessful. What do you say?
Two departments with very different cultures are being merged under your leadership. What do you say at the first joint meeting?
A neighbour wants your support for a petition you consider poorly thought through. What do you say to her?
You're asked to give a short speech thanking volunteers after a demanding festival season. What do you say?
A colleague keeps dismissing your suggestions in meetings with a slight smile. What do you say to him in private?
A patron complains that your library's new self-service system excludes older visitors. What do you say to him?
A promising candidate has asked for a salary well beyond your budget. What do you say to keep her interested?
During a seminar, you disagree with a highly respected professor's interpretation of the evidence. What do you say?
A client wants the project scope expanded without changing the agreed fee. What do you say to her?
You're asked to explain your company's new sustainability policy to a room of sceptical suppliers. What do you say?
A friend's wedding speech, which you've been asked to review, contains jokes that could offend. What do you say?
A fellow committee member keeps making decisions without consulting anyone else. What do you say to him?
You must tell a talented intern that there's no permanent position for him at the moment. What do you say?
A guest speaker cancels an hour before your event, and the audience is already seated. What do you say?
A media student asks you to explain how your industry has changed in the last decade. What do you say?
Your manager suggests you take on a high-profile project that would leave little time for your current clients. What do you say?
An architect's design for your home extension exceeds your budget by a considerable margin. What do you say to her?
A colleague has asked you to mentor her, but you're already stretched thin. What do you say?
Parents at your child's school want to scrap the annual concert to save money. What do you say at the meeting?
A partner organisation wants to delay a joint project indefinitely. What do you say to their director?
You need to persuade a reluctant landlord to let you convert a spare room into a studio. What do you say?
A cousin asks for your honest opinion on whether to leave a secure job for an uncertain creative career. What do you say?
A client complains, with some justification, that your team's communication has been patchy recently. What do you say to her?
A tour group you're leading is frustrated by a cancelled excursion. What do you say to them?
You're presenting a proposal, and a senior manager interrupts to say it has been tried before. What do you say?
Your sports club has been offered sponsorship by a company whose values some members question. As chair, what do you say?
You must explain to a frustrated customer why a discontinued product cannot be replaced. What do you say?
A colleague's reports have become noticeably careless over recent weeks. What do you say to him?
A recruiter asks you to justify why your salary expectations are higher than the advertised range. What do you say?
You've been asked to host a panel of experts who are known to disagree sharply. What do you say to open it?
A neighbour asks you to sign a letter objecting to a new playground, which you actually support. What do you say?
Your research team has produced results that contradict your client's expectations. What do you say when presenting them?
A long-standing member of your choir resists every change to the repertoire. What do you say to him?
A start-up founder asks you to invest, but her projections seem overly optimistic. What do you say?
You're asked to comment on a draft policy that seems well-intentioned but impractical. What do you say to its author?

C2.situation: A celebrated colleague has privately asked you to soften criticism of her work in a review you are about to publish. What do you say?
You must persuade a sceptical board that a costly but intangible investment in staff wellbeing will pay off. What do you say?
After a turbulent year, a brilliant but disorganised business partner asks whether your partnership should continue. What do you say?
At a literary festival, an audience member accuses your novel of trivialising a historical period in front of a packed hall. What do you say?
You are asked to deliver the closing remarks at a conference whose sessions revealed deep disagreement. What do you say?
A rival bidder proposes a joint venture that would benefit both firms but compromise your independence. What do you say?
A protege has accepted a prestigious offer from a competitor and asks for your blessing. What do you say to him?
A philanthropic foundation offers funding contingent on your research reaching conclusions it favours. What do you say to its director?
You must reconcile two senior partners whose longstanding feud is now jeopardising a major account. What do you say?
A distinguished audience at an awards ceremony expects you to accept an honour you feel ambivalent about. What do you say?
At a reception, you meet an eminent critic who panned your exhibition in terms you considered unfair. What do you say?
You are asked to adjudicate between two departments whose competing claims are each partly justified. What do you say?
A long-time collaborator wants to take your joint project in a commercial direction you find distasteful. What do you say?
A graduate student asks whether to pursue an academic career in a field with few permanent posts. What do you say?
The heir to a family business asks you to explain candidly why the firm's reputation has declined. What do you say?
As artistic director, you must justify dropping a beloved but loss-making production to the company. What do you say?
A peer insists on a methodological shortcut that you believe would compromise the integrity of your joint findings. What do you say?
Your client wants to celebrate a merger publicly before the terms have been finalised. What do you say to dissuade her?
At a public lecture, someone asks you to predict the outcome of a debate you consider genuinely unresolved. What do you say?
A former classmate, now your subordinate, assumes your shared past will exempt him from scrutiny. What do you say to him?
You are asked to introduce a speaker whose views you respect but fundamentally disagree with. What do you say?
A fiercely independent village community resists a tourism scheme that would revive its economy. As consultant, what do you say at the meeting?
A grant committee asks you to defend an interdisciplinary project that sits awkwardly between established fields. What do you say?
A colleague's brilliant but caustic emails are quietly alienating overseas partners. What do you say to her, without causing offence?
A collector offers to lend a masterpiece to your museum on terms that would effectively dictate its display. What do you say?
A jury you chair is split between a safe choice and a daring but uneven work. What do you say to the jurors?
A senior engineer insists the design is sound, yet your own calculations suggest a marginal flaw. What do you say?
You must explain to a loyal workforce why automation will transform, though not eliminate, their roles. What do you say?
During a podcast interview, the host invites you to disparage your former employer, which you'd rather not do. What do you say?
A trusted adviser urges you to accept a lucrative offer that you suspect would compromise your editorial freedom. What do you say?
A charity you advise wants to adopt aggressive fundraising tactics that might alienate supporters. What do you say to the trustees?
An eminent composer asks your honest opinion of a late work most critics consider a decline. What do you say?
The owners of a historic hotel want to modernise it in ways that would erase its character. As their consultant, what do you say?
You must convince a cautious publisher that your deliberately unconventional debut novel will find a devoted readership. What do you say?
A family member asks you to arbitrate a delicate dispute over the shared use of a holiday home. What do you say?
In your first meeting, the newly appointed chief executive asks for your unvarnished assessment of the company's culture. What do you say?
Your co-author wishes to respond to a hostile review with a public rebuttal you think would backfire. What do you say?
A sponsor demands last-minute changes to an exhibition that would distort the artist's intentions. What do you say to the sponsor?
An apprentice whose talent outstrips his discipline asks why he has been passed over for promotion. What do you say?
A delegation from a partner university proposes a joint degree whose standards you suspect would be diluted. What do you say?
At a farewell dinner, you are asked to speak about a departing colleague with whom you had a famously difficult relationship. What do you say?
